correctness.rationale: The complete facet orders for n=13 and n=14 are checked against exhaustive enumerations, and their shelling intersection conditions hold at every step; a logically separate maximal-intersection checker corroborates them. Exact full simplicial boundary ranks over F_2 give nonzero subtop homology for n=9..12. For n>=15 the correctly parameterized Chauhan--Shukla Theorem 1.4 supplies shellability. Boundary n<=8 follows from completeness and antipodal-pair structure. A pure shellable complex cannot have subtop reduced homology. The homotopy ranks for n13,14 are counted from spanning facets; the all-n tail is explicitly credited to published work. Finite computation is exhaustive exactly where applied and does not stand in for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact new cutoff at p=3 closes the n=13 and n=14 gap expressly left open by the parameter n>=6p-3 in Chauhan--Shukla Theorem 1.4. Complete facet certificates prove those shelling cases, whereas exact subtop homology establishes sharp failure n=9..12. Direct comparison of parameters and conclusions with relevant published cut-complex and representation works revealed no implication covering these two boundary cases. Residual unindexed duplication risk remains.
residual_risks: Unindexed independent shelling of n=13 or n=14 could exist under other terminology.
The squared-cycle paper was compared by exponent and the 2026 paper rather than exhaustively read; it does not have the relevant p=3 parameter.
No external independent scientific audit was performed.

value.rationale: The work proves the p=3 case of the concrete sharp 4p+1 threshold conjecture recorded in Chauhan--Shukla 2026: it closes the two missing shellability instances n=13 and n=14 and supplies rigorous obstructing homology below n=13. This is a natural boundary classification supported by explicit reproducible finite shelling certificates, not an arbitrary small numerical improvement or a restatement of the published large-n theorem.
